statement: a hot-wire-assisted ALD process deposits low-resistivity molybdenum from MoCl2O2 and atomic hydrogen, with self-limiting growth over a wide window of 150–450 °C
molecular hydrogen deposits nothing; atomic hydrogen is needed to reduce MoCl2O2, and the growth per cycle decays quickly as the hot-wire temperature falls and stops with the wire off
at 350 °C and above the films are nearly pure molybdenum with a few atomic percent of oxygen and traces of carbon, chlorine, hydrogen and nitrogen
no substrate selectivity or pronounced nucleation delay appeared on Si, SiO2, Si3N4, SiC, Al2O3, HfO2 or low-k SiOC
thickness and sheet resistance vary little within a central circle of the wafer, the nonuniformity rising toward the edge where atomic hydrogen, admitted above the centre, arrives less

at 250 °C and below more oxygen and chlorine enter the film, the growth per cycle rises, the optical constants change, density and crystallinity fall and resistivity rises: atomic hydrogen no longer strips the ligands fully
self-limiting growth spans 150–450 °C, but low-resistivity Mo needs 250 °C or more
ALD's self-limiting reactions give the thickness control, uniformity and conformality interconnects need, but a BEOL-compatible Mo ALD process was missing

at 350 °C the growth per cycle saturates with the MoCl2O2 and the atomic-hydrogen pulse times, rises as the MoCl2O2 purge shortens (a CVD contribution) and ignores the atomic-hydrogen purge, since atomic hydrogen recombines fast
the standard cycle 1/15/29/15 s sits near saturation; the long atomic-hydrogen pulse ensures reduction, which the growth per cycle alone may not show
sequential MoCl2O2 pulses without atomic hydrogen saturate the thickness over the whole window: chemisorption is self-limiting
the growth per cycle is about constant over the upper window for ALD and for CVD, several times higher for CVD, and rises toward lower temperatures; SE and XRR agree
the higher CVD growth per cycle points to gas-phase reactions or surface reactions enhanced by both reactants being present together

on SiO2 the steady regime starts after the first few nanometres; the growth-per-cycle transient suggests inhibited nucleation, yet the extrapolated thickness intercept is positive, as for enhanced growth, so the nature of nucleation stays open

mass spectrometry shows HCl leaving during the MoCl2O2 pulse and water during the atomic-hydrogen pulse: chemisorption goes through surface hydrogen and chloride ligands, and atomic hydrogen removes the oxygen and remaining chlorine

TOF-ERDA of a 20 nm film grown at 350 °C shows oxygen only at the surface oxide and the native SiO2 interface; the oxygen share climbs steeply toward lower temperatures, and chlorine appears at the lowest
SIMS puts the O, Cl, C, N and Si contaminants of the 350 °C ALD film near 1e20 atoms per cm3; CVD films gain oxygen toward lower temperatures, above 1e22 at 250 °C, tens of atomic percent

the resistivity approaches a bulk-like value in the thickest film and rises sharply below the electron mean free path of Mo; against temperature it rises at the low end for ALD and earlier for CVD, with the oxygen uptake

other Mo ALD works reached lower resistivities only at far higher temperatures, and a much higher one at a low temperature, so the value here, at a moderate temperature, is low and in line with the temperature trend
GIXRD of the 350 °C film shows the (110), (200) and (211) peaks of body-centred cubic Mo; the 150 °C film shows only the substrate peak and is amorphous, which also raises its resistivity

in SiO2-capped Si trenches of aspect ratio 2:1 to 10:1 the sidewall and bottom films keep most of the top thickness in the 3:1 trench, the bottom a little less; conformality falls with the aspect ratio, presumably through hydrogen recombination and hindered diffusion
the FFT rings of the TEM image match the d spacings of body-centred cubic Mo

EDX shows Mo reaching the bottom of a narrow trench with about twice the oxygen share there; atomic hydrogen likely recombines on the walls, so pure Mo deep in HAR structures may need longer atomic-hydrogen pulses
the electron mean free path of molybdenum is 11.2 nm
